messages:
marta (ML Eng): Quick heads-up — onboarding run for boreas-35k-int3 showed reproducible context divergence on concatenated system+user prefixes. :eyes:
ashok (research): Ugh, is this the usual prefilling ghost token thing?
sara (infra): Logs? which stage does it diverge — prefill or decode?
marta (ML Eng): Repro steps inline: I push two messages A and B (A system prompt, B user prompt). With FP16/INT8 everything matches. With int3 quant profile the KV indexes shift after token 2047 and outputs start to hallucinate. Minimal repro attached below.
marta (ML Eng): "```
# repro script (pseudo)
load_model('boreas-35k', quant='int3-profile-v2')
ctx = sys_prompt + user_prompt
out1 = model.generate(ctx, max_new_tokens=200)
# compare with same prompts on fp16
```"
ashok (research): Interesting — so divergence only after ~2k tokens, suggests RoPE index wrap or misapplied rotary scale in quant path. Did you check tokenization consistency between runs?
marta (ML Eng): Yup — same tokenizer binary. I also dumped token ids; they match. The KV write/read indices show an off-by-4 in a few shards post-2047 (see snippet).
marta (ML Eng): "```
KV_WRITE_IDX shard0: 2044 -> 2052
KV_READ_IDX  shard0: 2048 -> 2056
# mismatch only in int3 runs
```"
sara (infra): Could this be a packing/alignment issue in the int3 kernel (packing 3-bit lanes into 32-bit words)? We had similar with int4 pack offset before.
devon (platform): Assigning repro to me. Can you paste the exact model checksum and quant config? I want to spin the same image on a dedicated node.
marta (ML Eng): model_digest: sha256:bb9a1c...; quant: int3-v2.cfg (scale-per-channel, bias-preserve=false). I ran on a1-gpu-dedicated (cuda12, driver 535).
ashok (research): Hypothesis: the quant kernel's vectorized memcpy uses word-aligned loops that assume even-shard sizes; for certain long contexts the rotary rotation offsets get applied to wrong KV positions when a pack boundary crosses the window wrap. That would produce deterministic shift at a fixed global index (like 2048).
ashok (research): Quick patch idea: add a unit test that forces odd pack remainder sizes and checks that kv_read(k) == kv_write(k) after prefill across a boundary.
marta (ML Eng): I also ran eval harness (goldset long-context QA) and got >12% F1 drop on int3 vs fp16 past 3k tokens. Benchbot output: "```
benchbot: boreas-35k fp16 @ 3k tokens: EM=82.1 F1=79.3
benchbot: boreas-35k int3 @ 3k tokens: EM=69.4 F1=67.8
```"
sara (infra): If it's a pack-border bug we should mitigate with a software workaround: force context chunking that avoids crossing pack boundaries (ugly) or fallback to int4 for long-prefill requests until fixed. Which is less disruptive?
devon (platform): Fallback sounds reasonable. We can add a routing policy: if request.prefill_len > 2000 && model.quant == 'int3', route to int4 variant. Don't want customers hit this silently.
marta (ML Eng): Agreed. For immediate triage I'm going to: 1) add unit test for pack remainders (ashok), 2) instrument KV indices in runtime with diagnostics dump when shard mismatch detected (sara), 3) add routing fallback to int4 for long-prefill on staging (devon). I'll open PRs.
ashok (research): I'll start on unit test and see if I can produce a minimal C repro that demonstrates memcpy misalignment.
sara (infra): I'll add a temporary metric/kvcorr counter and a trace log when kv_write != kv_read. Pushing to staging tomorrow.
devon (platform): I'll add the routing rule and a rollout plan (canary 5% -> 25%). Also create a check that emits a customer-visible warning on routes that hit int3 long-prefill fallback.
marta (ML Eng): Thanks team. I've created a short issue with the artifacts: https://redwood.internal/issues/INFR-9382 and pushed the minimal repro to /mnt/artifacts/boreas-int3-kv-misalign.tar.gz. Assigning owners: ashok for test, sara for runtime instrument, devon for routing fallback. Will update when I have the unit test failing locally. :thumbsup:
benchbot: Scheduled nightly long-prefill smoke against staging with int3 variants — will post results in this thread tomorrow.
